bibl.title: Spike sorting for large, dense electrode arrays

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how to recover the firing times of individual neurons from the raw voltage recorded by a dense electrode array - the step that manufactures the single unit
span.quote: The process of using these waveforms to decipher the firing times of the recorded neurons is known as “spike sorting”

span.label: whether a practical system can sort high-channel-count data at error rates comparable to tetrode methods, in human and computer time a working lab will accept
span.quote: While the spike sorting problem has attracted considerable theoretical research, our goal was to produce a practical system that can be immediately used by working neurophysiologists. The ability to process large datasets (millions of spikes in hundreds of dimensions) in reasonable human and computer time was deemed essential; error rates comparable to those of commonly-used tetrode methods were deemed acceptable.

span.label: a three-stage pipeline (masked detection, masked EM clustering, guided manual curation) reaching about 5% error, plus a measurement of how much of the result depends on which human curates it
span.quote: However, use of this technology requires the development of techniques for decoding the spike times of the recorded neurons, from the raw data captured from the probes. Here, we present a set of novel tools to solve this problem, implemented in a suite of practical, user-friendly, open-source software. We validate these methods on data from the cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus of rat, mouse, macaque, and marmoset, demonstrating error rates as low as 5%.

span.label: method
span.quote: Here, we present a set of novel tools to solve this problem, implemented in a suite of practical, user-friendly, open-source software.

span.label: spike sorting for high-density electrode arrays
span.quote: Here we describe a system for the spike sorting of high-channel count electrode data, implemented in a suite of freely available software.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We have produced a software suite for spike sorting of data from large, dense electrode arrays.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: noise on many uninformative channels swamps signal on few informative channels, so Gaussian-mixture clustering breaks down as dimensionality grows
span.quote: The first is the “curse of dimensionality”: in high dimensions, noise measured on the large number of uninformative channels will swamp signals measured on the smaller number of informative channels.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: probabilistically disenfranchising low-mask channels removes their contribution to cluster assignment and so prevents threshold-crossing artefacts from generating spurious clusters
span.quote: Channels with low mask values are thus “disenfranchised”, and do not contribute to cluster assignment; the probabilistic nature of this disenfranchisement means false clusters are not created when amplitudes cross an arbitrary threshold.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: requiring a strong-threshold crossing inside each weak-threshold connected component discards isolated noise islands while merging weakly connected regions of one spike
span.quote: The dual-threshold approach avoids spurious detection of small noise events, since isolated islands in which only the weak threshold is exceeded are not retained.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: cost scales with unmasked channels per spike rather than total channels, which is why the method stays tractable as arrays grow
span.quote: The computational complexity of this algorithm is better than that of the traditional EM algorithm, scaling with the mean number of unmasked channels per spike (which does not increase for larger arrays), rather than the total number of channels.

span.label: overlapping spikes are separated not by their features, which are nearly identical, but by which channels they appear on - the mask vector
span.quote: Second, a “mask vector” is computed from the peak spike amplitude on each detected channel, rescaled and clipped so channels outside the connected component have mask 0, and channels with amplitude above θ s have mask 1. The mask vector allows temporally overlapping spikes to be clustered as separate cells.

span.label: the curse of dimensionality: on a large array the noise on uninformative channels outweighs the signal on the few informative ones
span.quote: The first is the “curse of dimensionality”: in high dimensions, noise measured on the large number of uninformative channels will swamp signals measured on the smaller number of informative channels.

span.label: masked EM disenfranchises low-mask channels probabilistically, so no false cluster is created when an amplitude happens to cross a threshold
span.quote: To solve this problem, we designed a novel method, the “masked EM algorithm” 30 . This algorithm fits the data as a mixture of Gaussians, but with each feature vector replaced by a virtual ensemble in which features with masks near zero are replaced by a noise distribution (see Methods). Channels with low mask values are thus “disenfranchised”, and do not contribute to cluster assignment; the probabilistic nature of this disenfranchisement means false clusters are not created when amplitudes cross an arbitrary threshold.

span.label: two thresholds rather than one: the weak one prevents a spike being split by noise, the strong one prevents noise being kept as a spike
span.quote: The dual-threshold approach avoids spurious detection of small noise events, since isolated islands in which only the weak threshold is exceeded are not retained. Conversely, spikes will not be erroneously split due to noise, as areas joined by weak threshold crossings are merged.

span.label: the human cost of curation is quadratic in clusters unless the software orders the candidate merges, which makes it linear
span.quote: Specifically, if N clusters are produced automatically, it is impractical for a human operator to inspect all order N

span.label: complexity scales with unmasked channels per spike, a quantity that does not grow as arrays get bigger
span.quote: The computational complexity of this algorithm is better than that of the traditional EM algorithm, scaling with the mean number of unmasked channels per spike (which does not increase for larger arrays), rather than the total number of channels.

span.label: Clustering can still take hours or days on large datasets with a single-core machine.
span.quote: KlustaKwik is several orders of magnitude faster than standard mixture of Gaussians fitting; nevertheless, when running on large datasets, it can take hours or even days to complete on a standard single-core machine.

span.label: Spikes that overlap in both space and time cannot be resolved by the detection algorithm.
span.quote: While the current algorithm can detect the majority of temporally overlapping spikes, which occur on distinct sets of channels, it cannot resolve spikes that overlap in both space and time.

span.label: Operators' judgements of which clusters count as well-isolated units are subjective, so the pipeline still depends on a non-reproducible human step.
span.quote: We found that experienced operators tended to make similar judgements during the manual curation process, but that their judgements of which units were well-isolated were subjective.

span.label: spikes that overlap in both space and time cannot be resolved at all
span.quote: A second opportunity for improvement regards the detection of spatiotemporally overlapping spikes. While the current algorithm can detect the majority of temporally overlapping spikes, which occur on distinct sets of channels, it cannot resolve spikes that overlap in both space and time.

span.label: ground truth is simulated, and rests on the assumption that the extracellular medium is a linear conductor so waveforms can simply be added
span.quote: We created a simulated ground truth dataset by repeatedly adding the spikes of a “donor cell” identified in one recording, to a second “acceptor” recording made with same probe; since the extracellular medium is a linear conductor 26 , addition of spike waveforms serves as a sufficient model for overlapping spikes.

span.label: the bursting interspike intervals that make real spike trains hard were deliberately not simulated
span.quote: The interspike intervals typical of bursting neurons were not simulated as this does not affect the spike detection or clustering process; instead, hybrid spikes were added regularly at rates in the range 2-4 spikes per second.

span.label: which clusters count as well-isolated single units is not reproducible between operators
span.quote: For all operators apart from one of the novices, consistency was extremely high for those spikes identified as good by at least one operator ( Fig. 7e,f ); nevertheless the judgement of whether a cluster should be considered well-isolated varied between operators

span.label: the waveform changes that force manual correction have resisted mathematical modelling
span.quote: Extracellular array recordings are subject to numerous sources of error including electrode drift, overlapping spikes, and the fact that neuronal spike waveforms are not constant, but change according to firing patterns including but not limited to bursting 27 - 29 . While most working neurophysiologists have a good understanding of these potential artifacts, formalizing this knowledge into a reliable mathematical model has proved challenging.

span.label: runtime can reach hours or days on a single core
span.quote: The first of these concerns execution time. KlustaKwik is several orders of magnitude faster than standard mixture of Gaussians fitting; nevertheless, when running on large datasets, it can take hours or even days to complete on a standard single-core machine.

span.label: template matching, which would solve the overlap problem, is blocked less by the algorithm than by what it would do to the curation step
span.quote: While recent research suggests that certain forms of template matching may succeed at least for tetrode data in vivo 18 , 21 , such methods are not at present widely applied to in vivo recordings, and numerous challenges need to be overcome, most critically regarding the manual curation step.

span.label: the EM algorithm for mixtures of Gaussians, modified so that uninformative dimensions are disenfranchised rather than weighted
span.quote: To solve this problem, we designed a novel method, the “masked EM algorithm” 30 . This algorithm fits the data as a mixture of Gaussians, but with each feature vector replaced by a virtual ensemble in which features with masks near zero are replaced by a noise distribution (see Methods). Channels with low mask values are thus “disenfranchised”, and do not contribute to cluster assignment; the probabilistic nature of this disenfranchisement means false clusters are not created when amplitudes cross an arbitrary threshold.

span.label: the flood fill, used to grow a spike as a connected component in space and time
span.quote: Specifically, spikes are detected as spatiotemporally connected components, in which the filtered signal exceeds a “weak threshold” θ w for every point, and in which at least one point exceeds a “strong threshold”

span.label: the Fowlkes-Mallows index, used here to score agreement between two human operators rather than between two clusterings
span.quote: We separately assessed consistency on spikes that all operators had identified be in “good” clusters, on spikes that at least one operator had identified to be in a good cluster, and on all remaining spikes. Similarity was assessed with the Fowlkes-Mallows index 31 , which gives a score between 1 for complete agreement, and 0 for complete disagreement.

span.label: the precedent that automatic methods in data-intensive science run under human supervision
span.quote: A similar situation arises in many fields of data-intensive science: in electron microscopic connectomics, for example, automatic methods can only be used under the supervision of human operators

span.label: every added spike displaced by a RANDOM SUB-SAMPLE OFFSET via cubic spline interpolation before being written into the simulated data
span.quote: To ensure that the simulated data tested the ability of our software to realign spikes to subsample resolution, each added spike was shifted by a random subsample offset using cubic spline interpolation.

span.label: ground truth here = SIMULATED - a known cell's waveforms added into another recording - not intracellular recording of the same neuron; the word is used for both in this literature
span.quote: We created a simulated ground truth dataset by repeatedly adding the spikes of a “donor cell” identified in one recording, to a second “acceptor” recording made with same probe; since the extracellular medium is a linear conductor 26 , addition of spike waveforms serves as a sufficient model for overlapping spikes.

span.label: well-isolated single unit = a cluster an operator accepts; the paper shows this judgement is not shared between operators, so the term does not denote a fixed object
span.quote: For all operators apart from one of the novices, consistency was extremely high for those spikes identified as good by at least one operator ( Fig. 7e,f ); nevertheless the judgement of whether a cluster should be considered well-isolated varied between operators

span.label: manual curation = correcting the automatic clustering, not selecting data; it is a required step of the measurement, not a post-hoc filter
span.quote: This last step is necessary because although fully automatic spike sorting would be a powerful tool, the output of current algorithms cannot be accepted without human verification.

span.label: mask vector = which channels a spike appeared on, rescaled to [0,1]; distinct from the feature vector, which is the PCA summary of its shape
span.quote: Second, a “mask vector” is computed from the peak spike amplitude on each detected channel, rescaled and clipped so channels outside the connected component have mask 0, and channels with amplitude above θ s have mask 1. The mask vector allows temporally overlapping spikes to be clustered as separate cells.

span.label: theoretical optimum = the Best Ellipsoid Error Rate, a quadratic decision boundary fitted to ground truth and cross-validated - a benchmark, not a bound on any possible algorithm
span.quote: To estimate the theoretical optimum performance that could be expected, we used the Best Ellipsoid Error Rate (BEER) measure 8 , which fits a quadratic decision boundary using ground truth data, and evaluates its performance with cross-validation, varying the parameters of the classifier to obtain an ROC curve showing optimal performance.

span.label: builds-on → KlustaKwik, first version (tetrode-oriented hard EM mixture-of-Gaussians program released in 2000)
span.quote: The first version of this program was designed for tetrode data, implemented a hard EM algorithm for maximum-likelihood fitting of a mixture of arbitrary-covariance Gaussians, and was released in 2000 but not specifically described in a published manuscript.

span.label: builds-on → Klusters manual spike-sorting environment (ref. 13)
span.quote: To ensure rapid adoption by the experimental community, we designed KlustaViewa’s user interface by the integrating novel features necessary for high-count probes into a user interface as similar as possible to existing manual spike sorting environments such as Klusters 13 .

span.label: builds-on → Best Ellipsoid Error Rate (BEER) measure (ref. 8)
span.quote: To estimate the theoretical optimum performance that could be expected, we used the Best Ellipsoid Error Rate (BEER) measure 8 , which fits a quadratic decision boundary using ground truth data, and evaluates its performance with cross-validation, varying the parameters of the classifier to obtain an ROC curve showing optimal performance.

span.label: extends → semi-automatic tetrode spike sorting, which reached 5% error against intracellular ground truth
span.quote: For tetrode data this semi-automatic process performs well, reaching error rates of 5% or lower, as assessed by ground truth data obtained with simultaneous intracellular recording

span.label: contradicts → the assumption that tetrode sorting methods carry over to large arrays
span.quote: However, spike sorting methods developed for tetrodes do not work for a newer generation of larger electrode arrays 15 , 16 . This failure occurs for two reasons. First, the automated component can fail in high dimensions, for example due to the “curse of dimensionality” that affects cluster analysis in high-dimensional spaces 17 . Second and perhaps more critically, the process of manual curation -- while manageable with low-count probes -- cannot scale to the high-count case without software that guides the operator to only those decisions that cannot be made reliably by a computer.

span.label: critiques → the practice of deciding by eye which units are well isolated
span.quote: We found that experienced operators tended to make similar judgements during the manual curation process, but that their judgements of which units were well-isolated were subjective. Fortunately, quantitative criteria exist for assessing the quality of unit isolation 32 , 33 , and we therefore recommend that these be used, rather than human judgements, when deciding which cells to include in further scientific analysis.

span.label: distinguishes-from → template-matching sorters validated on in vitro retinal arrays
span.quote: Template-matching algorithms have solved this problem in the case of in vitro retinal array data 38 , 39 , but these data are much less noisy than in vivo brain recordings.

span.label: critiques → the existing literature of proposed sorting methods, none of which was adopted
span.quote: While many different methods for spike sorting have been proposed (e.g. refs. 18 - 24 ), no method has yet solved these problems robustly enough to be widely adopted by the experimental community.

span.label: contradicts → the strategy of adding time as a clustering feature to track drift
span.quote: A strategy sometimes used to deal with nonstationarity is to include time as an additional feature in the cluster analysis algorithm, in principle allowing the algorithm to track slow changes in amplitude. To our surprise, we found that this actually worsened clustering performance, which could not always be overcome by manual curation

span.label: RETRACTED (DIRECTION REVERSED) · spike sorting —part-of→ manual curation
span.note: RETRACTED: DIRECTION REVERSED. The edge says spike sorting is part of manual curation. The paper says the opposite: 'Our spike sorting pipeline involves three steps: (1) spike detection and feature extraction, (2) cluster analysis, and (3) MANUAL CURATION.' Manual curation is a step OF spike sorting. Found while looking for a span naming both endpoints - the search for grounding surfaced a direction error. — direction is member-to-container: curation is the fourth step of the sorting process, not an optional extra
span.quote: While some labs use a fully manual system, lower error rates can be achieved with a semi-automated process 8 , consisting of four steps. First, spikes are detected, typically by high-pass filtering and thresholding. Second, each spike waveform is summarized by a compact “feature vector”, typically by principal component analysis. Third, these vectors are divided into groups corresponding to putative neurons using cluster analysis. Finally, the results are manually curated, to adjust any errors made by automatic algorithms

span.label: masked EM algorithm —contrasted-with→ classical EM algorithm
span.note: the same data: masked near the BEER optimum, classical above 50% error
span.quote: The masked EM algorithm’s performance on an example hybrid dataset was close to the optimum estimated by the BEER measure but the classical EM algorithm’s performance was poor, with error rates typically exceeding 50%

span.label: classical EM algorithm —causes→ curse of dimensionality
span.note: direction: the dimensionality is what defeats the classical fit
span.quote: The first is the “curse of dimensionality”: in high dimensions, noise measured on the large number of uninformative channels will swamp signals measured on the smaller number of informative channels.

The mask vector allows temporally overlapping spikes to be clustered as separate cells.

span.label: ground truth —operationalised-as→ hybrid datasets
span.note: the whole validation rests on this substitution, licensed by the linearity of the extracellular medium

span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span was about operator consistency. This sentence names both as the two outcomes of one decision - the operator 'EITHER accepts it as a WELL-ISOLATED neuron, OR rejects it as MULTIUNIT ACTIVITY or noise' - so the contrast is a forced choice rather than an observed difference. — the boundary the operator study found to be operator-dependent
span.quote: For all operators apart from one of the novices, consistency was extremely high for those spikes identified as good by at least one operator ( Fig. 7e,f ); nevertheless the judgement of whether a cluster should be considered well-isolated varied between operators

span.label: electrode drift —is-a→ nonstationarity
span.quote: Examination of data from acute recordings (where electrode drift is often stronger than with chronic probes), showed that the algorithm often tracked drift successfully, but in other cases split the spikes of a single drifty cell into multiple clusters requiring manual merging

span.label: bursting —is-a→ nonstationarity
span.quote: To model the variability of waveforms produced by a single neuron due to phenomena such as bursting 27 - 29 , we scaled each spike to a random amplitude in a range that varied by a factor of 2

span.label: electrode drift —causes→ manual curation
span.note: drift splits one cell into several clusters, which is what the human is there to merge
span.quote: Examination of data from acute recordings (where electrode drift is often stronger than with chronic probes), showed that the algorithm often tracked drift successfully, but in other cases split the spikes of a single drifty cell into multiple clusters requiring manual merging

span.label: Wizard —part-of→ manual curation
span.quote: We addressed this problem using a semi-automatic “Wizard,” that reduces the number of potential merges to order N . The Wizard works by presenting the operator with pairs of potentially mergeable clusters, ordered by a measure of pairwise cluster similarity.

span.label: silicon probes —contrasted-with→ tetrode
span.note: CRITERION, stated: overlapping spikes are extremely common on the dense probe and not on the tetrode
span.quote: The primary difference between spike detection for high count silicon probes and for tetrodes is that temporally overlapping spikes are extremely common in the former.

span.label: template matching —causes→ manual curation
span.note: what blocks the better algorithm is the curation step it would require, not its accuracy
span.quote: While recent research suggests that certain forms of template matching may succeed at least for tetrode data in vivo 18 , 21 , such methods are not at present widely applied to in vivo recordings, and numerous challenges need to be overcome, most critically regarding the manual curation step.

span.label: Best Ellipsoid Error Rate —contrasted-with→ masked EM algorithm
span.note: the benchmark the algorithm is measured against rather than a competing method
span.quote: The masked EM algorithm’s performance on an example hybrid dataset was close to the optimum estimated by the BEER measure but the classical EM algorithm’s performance was poor, with error rates typically exceeding 50%

span.quote: Our spike sorting pipeline involves three steps: (1) spike detection and feature extraction, (2) cluster analysis, and (3) manual curation.

span.note: RE-GROUNDS Rossant2016-spike-sorting-for-large-dense-electrode-arra[3]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Indeed, although the feature vectors of our two example spikes were very similar, their mask vectors are completely different ( Fig.

span.label: well-isolated —contrasted-with→ multiunit activity
span.note: RE-GROUNDS Rossant2016-spike-sorting-for-large-dense-electrode-arra[5]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Once satisfied that no more potential merges exist for the currently best unsorted cluster, the operator either accepts it as a well-isolated neuron, or rejects it as multiunit activity or noise, and the top-level iteration begins again.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Across all hybrid datasets, we found no significant difference between the total error of the masked EM algorithm and theoretical optimal performance (p = 0.8, t-test), but a significant difference between the performance of the Classical and Masked EM algorithms (p = 0.005, t-test; Fig. 4b ).

span.label: two-sample t-test
span.quote: A different type of nonstationarity, in which the hybrid cell simply stopped firing halfway through the recording, also had no effects on performance (p=0.75; two-sample t-test on total errors; Supplementary Fig. 16 ).

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: Feature vectors are computed for each channel separately by principal component analysis; the number of features per channel is a user settable parameter, with default value 3.

span.label: cross-validation
span.quote: To estimate the theoretical optimum performance that could be expected, we used the Best Ellipsoid Error Rate (BEER) measure 8 , which fits a quadratic decision boundary using ground truth data, and evaluates its performance with cross-validation, varying the parameters of the classifier to obtain an ROC curve showing optimal performance.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: Spike detection thresholds are specified as multiples of the standard deviation of the filtered signal; at the option of the user, a single threshold is used for all channels in order to avoid emphasizing noise from low-amplitude channels.

span.label: robust estimator (median absolute deviation)
span.quote: The standard deviation is computed with a robust estimator, median(| V |)/.6745, to avoid contamination by spike waveforms.

span.label: Bayesian Information Criterion
span.quote: We have found a modification of the Bayesian Information Criterion to deal with masked data works well in practice 30 .

span.label: maximum likelihood estimation (mixture of Gaussians)
span.quote: The first version of this program was designed for tetrode data, implemented a hard EM algorithm for maximum-likelihood fitting of a mixture of arbitrary-covariance Gaussians, and was released in 2000 but not specifically described in a published manuscript.

span.label: false discovery rate / true positive rate
span.term: false discovery rate / true positive rate
span.quote: For each dataset, we identified the cluster containing most hybrid spikes and computed the false discovery rate (fraction of spikes in the cluster that were not hybrids), and the true positive rate (fraction of all hybrid spikes assigned to the cluster).

span.label: Fowlkes-Mallows index (clustering agreement)
span.quote: Similarity was assessed with the Fowlkes-Mallows index 31 , which gives a score between 1 for complete agreement, and 0 for complete disagreement.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Across all hybrid datasets, we found no significant difference between the total error of the masked EM algorithm and theoretical optimal performance (p = 0.8, t-test), but a significant difference between the performance of the Classical and Masked EM algorithms (p = 0.005, t-test;

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: While some labs use a fully manual system, lower error rates can be achieved with a semi-automated process 8 , consisting of four steps. First, spikes are detected, typically by high-pass filtering and thresholding. Second, each spike waveform is summarized by a compact “feature vector”, typically by principal component analysis. Third, these vectors are divided into groups corresponding to putative neurons using cluster analysis. Finally, the results are manually curated, to adjust any errors made by automatic algorithms

span.label: mixture of Gaussians
span.quote: To solve this problem, we designed a novel method, the “masked EM algorithm” 30 . This algorithm fits the data as a mixture of Gaussians, but with each feature vector replaced by a virtual ensemble in which features with masks near zero are replaced by a noise distribution (see Methods). Channels with low mask values are thus “disenfranchised”, and do not contribute to cluster assignment; the probabilistic nature of this disenfranchisement means false clusters are not created when amplitudes cross an arbitrary threshold.

span.label: cross-validation
span.quote: To estimate the theoretical optimum performance that could be expected, we used the Best Ellipsoid Error Rate (BEER) measure 8 , which fits a quadratic decision boundary using ground truth data, and evaluates its performance with cross-validation, varying the parameters of the classifier to obtain an ROC curve showing optimal performance.

span.label: ROC curve
span.quote: To estimate the theoretical optimum performance that could be expected, we used the Best Ellipsoid Error Rate (BEER) measure 8 , which fits a quadratic decision boundary using ground truth data, and evaluates its performance with cross-validation, varying the parameters of the classifier to obtain an ROC curve showing optimal performance.

span.label: Bayesian Information Criterion
span.quote: To ensure the poor performance of the classical EM algorithm did not simply reflect incorrect parameter choice, we reran it for multiple values of the penalty parameter (which determines the number of clusters found), but this could not improve Classical EM performance.

span.label: Fowlkes-Mallows index
span.quote: We separately assessed consistency on spikes that all operators had identified be in “good” clusters, on spikes that at least one operator had identified to be in a good cluster, and on all remaining spikes. Similarity was assessed with the Fowlkes-Mallows index 31 , which gives a score between 1 for complete agreement, and 0 for complete disagreement.

span.label: Kullback-Leibler divergence
span.quote: The Kullback-Leibler divergence between two Gaussian distributions was unsuitable as it overweighted differences in covariance matrix relative to differences in the mean. However, good performance was obtained using a single step of the masked EM algorithm to compute the similarity of the mean of one cluster to each of the others

span.label: false discovery rate
span.quote: We conclude that the performance of the Masked EM algorithm is close to optimal for this clustering problem, yielding false positive and false discovery rates both of the order 5%.

span.label: geometric random walk
span.quote: We conclude that nonstationarity (at least of the type modelled here) does not present a serious problem to automatic sorting performance if time is not added as an additional feature, and if manual curation is performed when required.

span.label: Detection is close to optimal with a strong threshold of 4 SD, a weak threshold of 2 SD and a power weight of 2.
span.quote: We conclude that close to optimal performance can be obtained using a strong threshold of 4 SD, a weak threshold of 2 SD and a power weight of 2.

span.label: The masked EM clustering algorithm reaches roughly 5% false positive and false discovery rates, close to the theoretical optimum.
span.quote: We conclude that the performance of the Masked EM algorithm is close to optimal for this clustering problem, yielding false positive and false discovery rates both of the order 5%.

span.label: The classical EM algorithm failed on high-count probe data with error rates above 50%, whereas the masked EM algorithm matched the BEER-estimated optimum.
span.quote: The masked EM algorithm’s performance on an example hybrid dataset was close to the optimum estimated by the BEER measure but the classical EM algorithm’s performance was poor, with error rates typically exceeding 50% ( Fig. 4a ).

span.label: Human operators agreed with each other about which clusters to merge but disagreed about which clusters count as well-isolated, so quantitative isolation metrics should replace that judgement.
span.quote: We conclude that experienced operators are likely to make accurate and consistent judgements on cluster merging identification, but that the judgement on which clusters to term “good” is inconsistent; we therefore recommend that quantitative metrics 32 , 33 be used to determine isolation quality.

span.label: Spacing recording sites further apart than 40 μm substantially degrades sorting performance in rat cortex.
span.quote: We conclude that performance in rat cortex decreases substantially for site spacing larger the 40μm same-side site spacing of these test probes.

span.label: The two sides of a staggered shank act as largely independent probes, so the gain from two-sided shanks is more recorded units rather than better isolation of any one unit.
span.quote: We conclude that in staggered probes, the probe’s two sides function largely independently: the primary benefit of two-sided shanks is not to increase the isolation quality of a cell already well isolated on one side of the probe, but to record from a larger number of units.

span.label: Adding time as an extra clustering feature to track amplitude drift made clustering worse rather than better.
span.quote: To our surprise, we found that this actually worsened clustering performance, which could not always be overcome by manual curation ( Supplementary Fig. 15 ).

span.label: Manual curation time grows linearly with cluster count at roughly one minute per cluster and is independent of probe size.
span.quote: Using this software, the time taken for manual curation scales linearly with the number of clusters, with a scaling factor that varies between operators and is generally about 1 minute per cluster, regardless of probe size.

span.label: the masked EM algorithm is statistically indistinguishable from the theoretical optimum, while the classical EM is far from it
span.quote: Across all hybrid datasets, we found no significant difference between the total error of the masked EM algorithm and theoretical optimal performance (p = 0.8, t-test), but a significant difference between the performance of the Classical and Masked EM algorithms (p = 0.005, t-test;

span.label: false positive and false discovery rates are both about 5%
span.quote: We conclude that the performance of the Masked EM algorithm is close to optimal for this clustering problem, yielding false positive and false discovery rates both of the order 5%.

span.label: experienced operators agree on merges, but disagree on which clusters count as well isolated
span.quote: For all operators apart from one of the novices, consistency was extremely high for those spikes identified as good by at least one operator ( Fig. 7e,f ); nevertheless the judgement of whether a cluster should be considered well-isolated varied between operators

span.label: the authors therefore recommend quantitative isolation metrics in place of the human judgement
span.quote: We found that experienced operators tended to make similar judgements during the manual curation process, but that their judgements of which units were well-isolated were subjective. Fortunately, quantitative criteria exist for assessing the quality of unit isolation 32 , 33 , and we therefore recommend that these be used, rather than human judgements, when deciding which cells to include in further scientific analysis.

span.label: adding time as a clustering feature to track drift made performance worse, against expectation
span.quote: A strategy sometimes used to deal with nonstationarity is to include time as an additional feature in the cluster analysis algorithm, in principle allowing the algorithm to track slow changes in amplitude. To our surprise, we found that this actually worsened clustering performance, which could not always be overcome by manual curation

span.label: halving site density drops correct detection below 80%, so 40um same-side spacing is near the useful limit
span.quote: We conclude that performance in rat cortex decreases substantially for site spacing larger the 40μm same-side site spacing of these test probes.

span.label: the two sides of a staggered shank work independently: the gain is more units, not better isolation
span.quote: We conclude that in staggered probes, the probe’s two sides function largely independently: the primary benefit of two-sided shanks is not to increase the isolation quality of a cell already well isolated on one side of the probe, but to record from a larger number of units.

span.label: detection parameters optimal in cortex were also optimal in CA1
span.quote: We first generated an additional 5 hybrid cells using 10-site recordings from rat CA1 ( Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6 ). Good performance was again obtained; furthermore, the spike detection parameters found to be optimal in cortical data were also optimal in CA1 data.

span.label: the classical EM failure is not a parameter choice - rerunning across penalty values could not fix it
span.quote: To ensure the poor performance of the classical EM algorithm did not simply reflect incorrect parameter choice, we reran it for multiple values of the penalty parameter (which determines the number of clusters found), but this could not improve Classical EM performance.

span.label: spike sorting
span.quote: The process of using these waveforms to decipher the firing times of the recorded neurons is known as “spike sorting” 11 , 12 .

span.label: hybrid spikes / hybrid dataset
span.quote: We refer to the spikes added to the acceptor dataset as “hybrid spikes”, and the result as a “hybrid dataset”.

span.label: masked EM algorithm

span.label: mask vector

span.label: the Wizard (semi-automatic merge guide)
span.quote: We addressed this problem using a semi-automatic “Wizard,” that reduces the number of potential merges to order N .

span.label: spike sorting
span.quote: The process of using these waveforms to decipher the firing times of the recorded neurons is known as “spike sorting”

span.label: masked EM algorithm
span.quote: To solve this problem, we designed a novel method, the “masked EM algorithm” 30 . This algorithm fits the data as a mixture of Gaussians, but with each feature vector replaced by a virtual ensemble in which features with masks near zero are replaced by a noise distribution (see Methods). Channels with low mask values are thus “disenfranchised”, and do not contribute to cluster assignment; the probabilistic nature of this disenfranchisement means false clusters are not created when amplitudes cross an arbitrary threshold.

span.label: mask vector
span.quote: Second, a “mask vector” is computed from the peak spike amplitude on each detected channel, rescaled and clipped so channels outside the connected component have mask 0, and channels with amplitude above θ s have mask 1. The mask vector allows temporally overlapping spikes to be clustered as separate cells.

span.label: Best Ellipsoid Error Rate
span.quote: To estimate the theoretical optimum performance that could be expected, we used the Best Ellipsoid Error Rate (BEER) measure 8 , which fits a quadratic decision boundary using ground truth data, and evaluates its performance with cross-validation, varying the parameters of the classifier to obtain an ROC curve showing optimal performance.

span.label: hybrid datasets
span.quote: We created a simulated ground truth dataset by repeatedly adding the spikes of a “donor cell” identified in one recording, to a second “acceptor” recording made with same probe; since the extracellular medium is a linear conductor 26 , addition of spike waveforms serves as a sufficient model for overlapping spikes.

span.label: Fowlkes-Mallows index
span.quote: We separately assessed consistency on spikes that all operators had identified be in “good” clusters, on spikes that at least one operator had identified to be in a good cluster, and on all remaining spikes. Similarity was assessed with the Fowlkes-Mallows index 31 , which gives a score between 1 for complete agreement, and 0 for complete disagreement.

span.label: curse of dimensionality
span.quote: The first is the “curse of dimensionality”: in high dimensions, noise measured on the large number of uninformative channels will swamp signals measured on the smaller number of informative channels.

span.label: detection thresholds and alignment power (θ w, θ s, p)
span.term: detection thresholds and alignment power (θ w, θ s, p)
span.quote: We measured performance as a function of three algorithm parameters ( θ w , θ s and p ), using four performance statistics.

span.label: fraction of hybrid spikes detected
span.quote: The first statistic was the fraction of hybrid spikes detected ( Fig. 3b ).

span.label: spike timing jitter
span.quote: The third statistic was timing jitter: the standard deviation of the difference between the detected and actual times of each hybrid spike ( Fig. 3d ).

span.label: mask accuracy
span.quote: The final statistic was mask accuracy ( Fig. 3e ), which measures how closely the detected mask vectors match those expected from the ground truth (see Methods).

span.label: electrode site density (site thinning)
span.quote: In the first (“site thinning”; Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2 ), the electrode was made less dense by omitting alternating channels on both sides.

span.label: cluster-number penalty parameter
span.quote: To ensure the poor performance of the classical EM algorithm did not simply reflect incorrect parameter choice, we reran it for multiple values of the penalty parameter (which determines the number of clusters found), but this could not improve Classical EM performance.

span.label: weak threshold
span.quote: Specifically, spikes are detected as spatiotemporally connected components, in which the filtered signal exceeds a “weak threshold” θ w for every point, and in which at least one point exceeds a “strong threshold”

span.label: strong threshold
span.quote: Specifically, spikes are detected as spatiotemporally connected components, in which the filtered signal exceeds a “weak threshold” θ w for every point, and in which at least one point exceeds a “strong threshold”

span.label: site spacing
span.quote: We conclude that performance in rat cortex decreases substantially for site spacing larger the 40μm same-side site spacing of these test probes.

span.label: operator experience
span.quote: We assessed the performance of 8 human operators (5 experienced spike-sorters, 3 novices) using this system ( Fig. 7a ). First, we asked whether the operators would correctly fix a misclustering that was produced by the masked EM algorithm in simulation of electrode drift (described further below). All experienced operators, and all but one of the novices did this correctly.

span.label: penalty parameter
span.quote: To ensure the poor performance of the classical EM algorithm did not simply reflect incorrect parameter choice, we reran it for multiple values of the penalty parameter (which determines the number of clusters found), but this could not improve Classical EM performance.

span.label: 5% — error rate the whole pipeline achieves on validation data across species and brain regions
span.quote: We validate these methods on data from the cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus of rat, mouse, macaque, and marmoset, demonstrating error rates as low as 5%.

span.label: 95% — proportion of ground-truth (hybrid) spikes correctly detected at the chosen parameters, with 0.5-sample timing jitter
span.quote: Furthermore, using these parameters yields around 95% correctly detected spikes, and spike timing jitter of 0.5 samples.

span.label: p = 0.8 — t-test comparing masked EM total error to theoretical optimum (no difference), versus p = 0.005 for masked vs classical EM
span.quote: Across all hybrid datasets, we found no significant difference between the total error of the masked EM algorithm and theoretical optimal performance (p = 0.8, t-test), but a significant difference between the performance of the Classical and Masked EM algorithms (p = 0.005, t-test; Fig. 4b ).

span.label: p=0.75 — two-sample t-test showing a cell that stopped firing halfway through the recording did not change total sorting error
span.quote: A different type of nonstationarity, in which the hybrid cell simply stopped firing halfway through the recording, also had no effects on performance (p=0.75; two-sample t-test on total errors; Supplementary Fig. 16 ).

span.label: below 80% — average correct spike-detection rate once alternating recording sites were removed (site thinning)
span.quote: Spike detection was strongly impacted, with correct detection rates dropping to an average of below 80% ( Supplementary Fig. 1 ).

span.label: over 320 scientists in 50 neurophysiology labs — size of the user base whose feedback shaped the software
span.quote: The techniques and software have been developed in a community-led manner, through extensive feedback from a user base of over 320 scientists in 50 neurophysiology labs.

span.label: over 10,000% — speed increase of the reimplemented KlustaKwik clustering program
span.quote: The program now implements a novel “masked EM algorithm” 30 designed for high-dimensional classification, as well as other features such as cache optimization resulting in a speed increase of over 10,000%.

span.label: 5% — false positive and false discovery rate of the masked EM algorithm on hybrid data
span.quote: We conclude that the performance of the Masked EM algorithm is close to optimal for this clustering problem, yielding false positive and false discovery rates both of the order 5%.

span.label: over 50% — error rate of the classical EM algorithm on the same data
span.quote: The masked EM algorithm’s performance on an example hybrid dataset was close to the optimum estimated by the BEER measure but the classical EM algorithm’s performance was poor, with error rates typically exceeding 50%

span.label: 4 SD and 2 SD — optimal strong and weak detection thresholds, with power weight 2
span.quote: We conclude that close to optimal performance can be obtained using a strong threshold of 4 SD, a weak threshold of 2 SD and a power weight of 2. Furthermore, using these parameters yields around 95% correctly detected spikes, and spike timing jitter of 0.5 samples.

span.label: 95% — spikes correctly detected at those settings, with 0.5 samples of timing jitter
span.quote: We conclude that close to optimal performance can be obtained using a strong threshold of 4 SD, a weak threshold of 2 SD and a power weight of 2. Furthermore, using these parameters yields around 95% correctly detected spikes, and spike timing jitter of 0.5 samples.

span.label: below 80% — correct detection after site thinning - the cost of halving electrode density
span.quote: In the first (“site thinning”; Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2 ), the electrode was made less dense by omitting alternating channels on both sides. We evaluated the performance of spike detection and clustering using the same hybrid spikes described earlier, but only on this subset of channels (the adjacency graph was modified to join any two channels that both connected to a missing channel). Spike detection was strongly impacted, with correct detection rates dropping to an average of below 80%

span.label: 40 — micron same-side site spacing beyond which performance in rat cortex falls off
span.quote: We conclude that performance in rat cortex decreases substantially for site spacing larger the 40μm same-side site spacing of these test probes.

span.label: about 1 minute per cluster — operator time for curation, linear in cluster count and independent of probe size
span.quote: Using this software, the time taken for manual curation scales linearly with the number of clusters, with a scaling factor that varies between operators and is generally about 1 minute per cluster, regardless of probe size. This software therefore allows for thorough manual curation of a dense-array recording in a few hours.

span.label: 8 — human operators tested, 5 experienced and 3 novices
span.quote: We assessed the performance of 8 human operators (5 experienced spike-sorters, 3 novices) using this system ( Fig. 7a ). First, we asked whether the operators would correctly fix a misclustering that was produced by the masked EM algorithm in simulation of electrode drift (described further below). All experienced operators, and all but one of the novices did this correctly.

span.label: 6 of 10 — hybrid cells detectable on only one side of a staggered probe
span.quote: Of the 10 hybrid cells analyzed, 6 were only detectable on one of the probe’s two sides, while the other 4 could be detected on both sides to a greater or lesser extent

span.label: over 320 scientists in 50 neurophysiology labs — the user base whose feedback shaped the software
span.quote: The techniques and software have been developed in a community-led manner, through extensive feedback from a user base of over 320 scientists in 50 neurophysiology labs.

span.label: 10-20 — simultaneously recorded cells a tetrode can reveal, against one or two for a sharp electrode
span.quote: Indeed, while a single sharp electrode can provide good isolation of one or two neurons, placing as few as four recording sites together in a “tetrode” can reveal the firing patterns of 10-20 simultaneously recorded cells
